finding.text: The task folder's own records (`session.jsonl`, `measure.json`, `past-work.md`) stop at commit `6a75aec62` and don't mention the two follow-up commits actually on the branch, `c1a853865` (server-guard heredoc fix) and `b308b21f0` (Processes: count dev servers by server, not by process) — both made directly by the parent `mastermind-resources` session after this task's own sub-session ended "without landing" (`session.jsonl:51`). Those two commits ARE logged, but only in `mastermind-resources/session.jsonl:1922`, not here. A fresh agent opening only this task folder would believe the fix stopped at `classify_leftover()` with 51 raw-process counting, and would not know the health line now counts server trees (`g.servers`) or that `server-guard.mjs` grew a `shell_segments()` heredoc/quote-aware splitter. This fails the "a fresh agent must be able to continue from the task folder alone" bar and rule 9/10 (document the structure, index everything you create).

Deliverable 2 explicitly says "Use a node script that reads the real state (the `/api/processes` endpoint on `http://127.0.0.1:8090` and the files), never a count by hand" — but `measure.json`'s own `method` field says the numbers came from "a one-shot PowerShell process sample... run through this worktree's PATCHED Processes.js", not from the `/api/processes` endpoint, and no script was committed anywhere under this task (checked `git log --all --diff-filter=A -- '*dev-server-count*'`: only `measure.json` and `session.jsonl` were ever added). The measurement is plausible but isn't reproducible or provably sourced from the live endpoint as asked, and nothing explains the deviation.

The task's own log (`session.jsonl:32`) and its reply to `mastermind-resources` both say "51 checks pass," but running `node Servex/processes.test.mjs` now (after the branch's full history, including the two later commits) prints 50 total checks, and `node .claude/hooks/server-guard.test.mjs` prints 61, not the "65/65" the parent's log line claims. Small, but a count that doesn't match a one-command rerun undercuts "compute, don't recall."

`measure.json`'s `counts_agree: false` is explained (a pre-existing `list_servers`/`procs/*.json` registry gap, 7 of 8 real servers are parent-gone orphans Servex never re-adopted) and is logged as out of scope rather than silently dropped — this matches the brief's own escape hatch ("if they are not, say why") and reads as a legitimate, well-reasoned call, not a gap.
